newsitem.title: USA: EU official softens stance on Boeing sales pact.
newsitem.headline: EU official softens stance on Boeing sales pact.

text.p: A key official of the European Union's competition section softened the stance of the EU Thursday against Boeing Co's exclusive provider agreements with two commercial airlines.

Speaking before an International Monetary Fund forum, Alexander Schaub, EU director-general for competition, was asked to square the opposition of the EU to Boeing's exclusive provider agreements in light of similar agreements some European companies have made.
Schaub, the number-two man in the competition area for the EU, gave a careful and detailed response.

But at the end he declined to insist that the exclusive provider agreements must be ended as a condition of EU approval of the merger: "Nobody can tell you today what would be the outcome of our European investigation and what will be the outcome of the American investigation here done by the FTC," he said.
"There's only one thing I can tell you with certainty today: that is, the deadline for the conclusion of the European investigation is the 31st of July," he said.

Earlier this year European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said flatly during a visit to Washington that the EU would not approve the merger of Boeing and McDonnell Douglas Corp unless Boeing's 20-year exclusive provider agreements with Delta Airlines and American Airlines were ended.
Schaub made the same point but in far softer terms.

"You could come to the idea that exclusive deals worsen, particularly long-term exclusive deals worsen the competitive situation and that without exclusive deals the situation may be perhaps slightly less unacceptable or slightly more acceptable," Schaub said.
Schaub, asked about the apparent differences between his views and those of Van Miert, said: "I think I have been extremely clear today and I have absolutely nothing to add."
